with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary atan2 angle tangent unit-circle angular-speed oscillation amplitude period sine cosine radian >}}

## 8.1 Which angle is the target at?

- A turret at (0, 0) must face a drone at d = (4, 4). Which angle?
- tan θ = d~y~ ÷ d~x~ = 1, so 45°. But (−4, −4) also gives 1: the
  division loses the signs.
- **atan2(y, x)** uses the signs of both parts. It gives the angle from
  −180° to 180°, right in every quadrant.
- (4, 4): 45°. (−4, 4): 135°. (−4, −4): −135°. (0, −3): −90°.
  (3, 5.2): tan ≈ 1.73, so 60°.
- In Unity: `Mathf.Atan2(d.y, d.x) * Mathf.Rad2Deg` (y first).

![Same slope, different angle.](images/atan2.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The order is (y, x). With (x, y), a drone at (4, 0) comes out at 90°
instead of 0°.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/turn-lab.html" poster="sims/turn-lab.png" title="Turn Lab: the angle to a target and the short turn" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Angles in Turn Lab"}
In **Turn Lab**, tap the targets (5, 0), (0, 4), (−3, 3) and (−3, −3).
Write the vector d and the angle from atan2 each time. Which quadrant is
each target in?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The angle to a target"}
The turret is at (0, 0). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="−45°|0°"}
A drone at (5, 5). Its angle?
:   45°

A drone at (−4, 4). Its angle?
:   135°

A drone at (−4, −4). Its angle?
:   −135°

A drone at (0, −3). Its angle?
:   −90°

Why is tan alone not enough?
:   it loses the signs of x and y
:::
:::

## 8.2 Turning the short way

- Facing 350°, target 10°: 10° − 350° = −340°, almost a full turn. The
  short way is **+20°**.
- Step 1: difference = target − facing.
- Step 2: more than 180° → subtract 360°; less than −180° → add 360°.
- \+ means turn left (anticlockwise); − means turn right (clockwise).
- Time = size of the turn ÷ turning speed. At 90° per second: 90° takes
  1 s, 135° takes 1.5 s.
- In Unity: `Mathf.DeltaAngle(350, 10)` gives 20.

![Turn the short way.](images/shortest-turn.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Without step 2, an enemy spins almost a full circle for a target just behind
its shoulder.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The short turn in Turn Lab"}
In **Turn Lab**, choose **Facing 350°**, tap (6, 1) and press **Turn**. Then
choose **Facing 170°** and tap (−6, −1). Write each short turn (left or
right, how many degrees) and its time.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Short turns"}
The turret turns at 90° per second. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="−340°|3 s"}
Facing 30°, target 120°. The short turn?
:   +90° (left)

Facing 350°, target 10°. The short turn?
:   +20° (left)

Facing 10°, target 340°. The short turn?
:   −30° (right)

Facing 170°, target −170°. The short turn?
:   +20° (left)

Facing 0°, target −135°. How long does the turn take?
:   1.5 s
:::
:::

## 8.3 Moving in a circle

- An orb circles a hero; a moon circles a planet.
- Position: **P(t) = C + r (cos θ, sin θ)**, with the centre C and the
  radius r.
- The angle grows at the **angular speed** ω: θ = ω × t.
- **Period**: one full turn takes T = 360° ÷ ω.
- C = (5, 5), r = 2, 90° per second: t = 0 (7, 5); 1 s (5, 7); 2 s (3, 5);
  3 s (5, 3); period 4 s.
- Moon: centre (0, 0), r = 4, 30° per second: after 1 s at (3.5, 2);
  period 12 s.

![The orb circles C = (5, 5).](images/orbit.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Multiply (cos θ, sin θ) by the radius, then add the centre.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/wave-lab.html" poster="sims/wave-lab.png" title="Wave Lab: circle, bob and sweep" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · An orbit in Wave Lab"}
In **Wave Lab**, choose **Orbit**, the amplitude 2 (the radius) and the
period 4 s. Step to 0, 1, 2 and 3 s and write the positions. Then set the
period to 8 s: what is the angular speed?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Orbits"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(7, 5)|(5, 5)"}
C = (5, 5), r = 2, 90° per second. Where is the orb at 1 s?
:   (5, 7)

The same orb at 2 s?
:   (3, 5)

An orb turns at 90° per second. Its period?
:   4 s

A moon turns at 30° per second. Its period?
:   12 s

Centre (0, 0), r = 4, angle 90°. The position?
:   (0, 4)
:::
:::

## 8.4 Bobbing up and down: oscillating motion

- A coin bobs; a lift goes up and down. This is an **oscillation**: back
  and forth around a middle, again and again.
- **y(t) = c + A sin(360° × t ÷ T)**: middle c, **amplitude** A,
  **period** T.
- At a quarter of T: the top, c + A. At three quarters: the bottom,
  c − A. At 0, half and full T: the middle.
- Lift y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4): 0 s → 2; 1 s → **5**; 2 s → 2;
  3 s → **−1**.
- Coin: middle 2, A = 0.5, T = 2 s: 0.5 s → 2.5; 1.5 s → 1.5.

![The lift: middle 2, amplitude 3, period 4 s.](images/sine-wave.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The amplitude is half of the whole movement: with A = 3, the lift moves
6 units from bottom to top.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The lift in Wave Lab"}
In **Wave Lab**, choose **Bob**, the amplitude 3 and the period 4 s. Step to
0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 s and write the heights. Then set the period to 8 s: when
is the lift at the top?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Bobbing"}
y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4). Choose the right answer. You can use an answer
more than once.

::: {.match extra="3|8 s"}
The height at 1 s.
:   5

The height at 3 s.
:   −1

The height at 2 s.
:   2

The period.
:   4 s

How many units does the lift move from bottom to top?
:   6
:::
:::

## 8.5 Sweeping back and forth: an angle that oscillates

- A searchlight sweeps a yard. Now the **angle** oscillates:
  angle(t) = 45° × sin(360° × t ÷ 4).
- The beam points along (cos angle, sin angle), as in lecture 7.
- 0 s: 0°, beam (1, 0). 1 s: 45°, beam (0.71, 0.71). 3 s: −45°, beam
  (0.71, −0.71).
- It covers 90° in all: the amplitude 45° to each side.
- A rocking boat: tilt = 10° × sin(360° × t ÷ 4); largest tilt 10° at 1 s.

![A searchlight sweeps from −45° to 45°.](images/searchlight.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Here the angle swings, not the position. Turn the angle into the direction
(cos, sin).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Sweep in Wave Lab"}
In **Wave Lab**, choose **Sweep**, the amplitude 45° and the period 4 s. Step
to 0, 1, 2 and 3 s and write the angle and the beam direction. A player
sneaks across the yard at −45° from the tower: when is the beam farthest
away?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The searchlight"}
angle = 45° × sin(360° × t ÷ 4). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(1, 0) at 1 s|180°"}
The angle at 1 s.
:   45°

The angle at 3 s.
:   −45°

The beam direction at 1 s.
:   (0.71, 0.71)

How many degrees does the light cover in all?
:   90°

The angle at 2 s.
:   0°
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Sky Lift {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Sky Lift** is a platform game. A hero waits on a cliff at the height 5.
Beside it, a lift floats up and down: y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4), with the
middle 2, the amplitude 3 and the period 4 s. The clock starts with the lift
at the middle, going up. A second ledge is lower, at the height −1. The hero
can step on only when the lift is level with a ledge.

{{< sim file="sims/sky-lift.html" poster="sims/sky-lift.png" title="Sky Lift: when is the lift level with the ledge?" kind="game" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · The lift"}
Sky Lift: y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4). Cliff at 5, low ledge at −1.
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="2 s|0 s"}
When is the lift level with the cliff for the first time?
:   1 s

When is the lift level with the low ledge for the first time?
:   3 s

Where is the lift at 2 s?
:   at the middle, 2

The highest point of the lift.
:   5
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · A second lift (harder)"}
Sky Lift. Lift 1: y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4), cliff at 5. Lift 2 is a
cabin on a wheel: centre (0, 3), radius 2, 90° per second, starting at 0°
(right). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="3 s|(2, 3)"}
After the first time at 1 s, when is lift 1 at the cliff again?
:   5 s

When is the wheel cabin at the top, (0, 5)?
:   1 s

Where is the wheel cabin at 2 s?
:   (−2, 3)

The period of the wheel.
:   4 s

A new lift has the period 8 s. When is it at the top for the first time?
:   2 s
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- atan2(y, x) gives the angle to a target in every quadrant.
- Turn the short way: target − facing, then bring it into −180° to 180°.
- Circle: P = C + r (cos θ, sin θ), with θ = ω t; the period is 360° ÷ ω.
- Bobbing: y = c + A sin(360° × t ÷ T); top at T ÷ 4, bottom at 3T ÷ 4.
- A sweeping light: the angle oscillates, and the beam is (cos, sin) of it.
